s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of seizures with altered mental status and history of recent substance use
salient_findings: History of left cerebral ischemic stroke and myocardial infarction 4 months ago
Diffuse bilateral cortical and subcortical edema on brain imaging
key_facts: Presented to the emergency department after a seizure
History of left cerebral ischemic stroke and myocardial infarction 4 months ago
Used synthetic cannabis before the seizure
Normal complete blood cell count, chemistry panel, aspirin level, acetaminophen level, alcohol level, and liver function tests
Urine drug screen positive for cannabinoids

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of seizures with altered mental status and history of recent substance use
salient_findings: History of left cerebral ischemic stroke and myocardial infarction 4 months ago
Diffuse bilateral cortical and subcortical edema on brain imaging
key_facts: Presented to the emergency department after a seizure
History of left cerebral ischemic stroke and myocardial infarction 4 months ago
Used synthetic cannabis before the seizure
Normal complete blood cell count, chemistry panel, aspirin level, acetaminophen level, alcohol level, and liver function tests
Urine drug screen positive for cannabinoids

differentials: primary angiitis of the central nervous system

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with seizures, altered mental status (Glasgow Coma Scale score of 9), and diffuse bilateral cortical and subcortical edema on imaging, in the context of recent synthetic cannabis use, is most consistent with encephalopathy.

rejected.label: stroke
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of stroke, the current presentation with seizures and encephalopathy is not typical for a new stroke.

rejected.label: ischemic stroke
rejected.why: Similar to stroke, the patient's symptoms and imaging findings are not consistent with a new ischemic stroke.

rejected.label: epilepsy
rejected.why: The patient has no prior history of seizure disorder, making new-onset epilepsy less likely.

rejected.label: moyamoya syndrome
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence in the vignette to suggest moyamoya syndrome, such as characteristic imaging findings or a history of recurrent strokes or seizures.
